title: Why college degrees are becoming worthless in 2026

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: In 2026, will college degrees still signal competence, or will they be outdated by AI and new learning models?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: AI tutors and nanodegree platforms now offer hyper-personalized skills training in weeks, outpacing traditional four-year programs.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: This risks deepening inequality — those who can’t afford or access these tools may be left behind in an automated economy.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Builders are creating open-source learning networks and micro-credentialing systems to democratize access and validate skills.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A future where learning is lifelong, collaborative, and driven by real-world impact, not just degrees.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future belongs to those who adapt — learning must evolve as fast as the world itself.

video_cue: A classroom with AI avatars guiding students through holographic simulations of real-world problem-solving scenarios.
